title: SEC Probes Nvidia’s Disclosures After Jensen Huang’s Departure
gist: The SEC has opened a civil inquiry into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors after Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation as CEO, with questions centering on Huang's relationships and Asian chip sales (including Singapore-based Megaspeed); California's AG has separately subpoenaed Nvidia over possible advanced-chip leakage to China, even as Nvidia reported $115.8B quarterly revenue, up 103%.

insights.claim: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is conducting a civil inquiry into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, according to The Wall Street Journal; the SEC declined to comment.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: An SEC disclosure probe adds headline and potential enforcement risk to Nvidia during a leadership transition; watch the upcoming quarterly filing for legal-proceedings language.
insights.locator: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia

insights.claim: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena examining whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors or the public about that risk.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A parallel state-level probe compounds regulatory exposure and ties Nvidia's governance questions to China export-control risk.
insights.locator: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced

insights.claim: Investor questions about Nvidia's disclosures focus on Jensen Huang's relationships and Asian chip sales; Nvidia previously denied Huang had an unusual relationship with Alice Huang, then an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Links the CEO departure to the Megaspeed chip-diversion question, raising the stakes of any finding that disclosures were inaccurate.
insights.locator: The Journal reported that investors have raised questions

insights.claim: Nvidia changed how it presented international sales last year and stopped separately disclosing sales to Singapore, per The Wall Street Journal.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Reduced geographic transparency is a likely regulatory focus; any restoration or restatement of Singapore sales data could be market-moving.
insights.locator: The Journal also reported that Nvidia changed

insights.claim: Nvidia announced on Nov. 12 that Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member effective immediately, and the board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while it considers internal and external successors.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: An abrupt founder-CEO exit with a CFO serving as interim CEO creates succession uncertainty; the permanent CEO pick is a key catalyst.

insights.claim: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, including $107.6 billion from its data-center segment.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Fundamentals remain exceptionally strong; the debate shifts to whether governance and export-control risk warrant a valuation discount.
insights.locator: The scrutiny comes as Nvidia’s data-center business

insights.claim: Nvidia's forthcoming full quarterly report typically updates risk factors, legal proceedings and internal controls over financial reporting, making it the next disclosure checkpoint on the SEC and California probes.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Read the upcoming quarterly filing for new risk-factor and internal-control language tied to the investigations.
insights.locator: Nvidia said it would file its full quarterly report
